column1: Standardized URNs (Uniform Resource Names): DataHub relies heavily on URNs as unique identifiers. Always use lowercase for platform names and environments to avoid duplicates (e.g., PROD vs prod).
Glossary Taxonomy (GlossaryNode and GlossaryTerm): Create a hierarchical structure for your business architecture.
Example: Node: Finance -> Node: Accounts_Payable -> Term: Invoice_Processing_(Business_Process).
Use Tags for quick, informal, or operational state flagging (e.g., Deprecated, PII, SourceOfRecord, Batch_ETL).
Use Glossary Terms for strictly defined, governed business concepts (e.g., Customer_Churn_Rate, Business_Capability).
How these new columns map into DataHub:
Source System (SOR): This maps directly to DataHub's DataPlatform entity (e.g., Oracle, Hive, Kafka, Tableau). It tells the catalog where the data lives.

Source URL: DataHub has a feature called Institutional Memory (or external links). You can attach these URLs directly to the Dataset or Dataflow entity so users can click out to the original git repository, Control-M console, or reporting dashboard.
If it's a Query (like SQL or Cypher), this is typically ingested into the ViewProperties or stored as a DataJob showing exactly how a dataset was transformed.
